record.paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can Dicke states |D^n_k>, the symmetric n-qubit states with k excitations distributed among n qubits, be made first-class resources for multiparty quantum key agreement by designing protocols that use them as the fundamental entangled resource and by proving security and fairness comparable to GHZ- and Bell-based schemes? In particular, how do the Dicke-state parameters (n,k) affect strong fairness under collusion, qubit efficiency, realistic key rates, noise and loss thresholds, and performance across star, tree, and hybrid architectures under device-dependent, measurement-device-independent, and semi-device-independent security models?

evidence.quote: Dicke states are a natural class of multipartite entangled states, characterized by a fixed number k of excitations distributed among n qubits.

The design and analyze Dicke-state-based MQKA protocols that achieve security and fairness guarantees comparable to today’s GHZ-based and Bell-based schemes naturally appears as an explicit open problem.

Yet there is no systematic understanding of how these properties translate into MQKA-specific goals such as strong fairness under collusion, qubit efficiency, and realistic key rates across different network architectures.

A concrete research direction is to construct client–server or hybrid MQKA protocols in which multipartite Dicke states (|D^k_n⟩) are the fundamental entangled resource, and to characterize their performance under the three axes identified in this review: network architecture, quantum resources, and security model.

Overall, establishing Dicke states as first-class MQKA resources—with tailored encoding rules, parameter-estimation strategies, and fairness proofs—remains an open problem that could significantly expand the toolkit for fairness-aware MQKA in realistic quantum networks.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1 be integers. The Dicke state |D^n_k⟩ is the symmetric n-qubit pure state defined by

  |D^n_k⟩ = C(n,k)^{−1/2} · Σ_{x ∈ {0,1}^n, |x|=k} |x⟩,

where the sum is over all binary strings of length n with Hamming weight exactly k. A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol among n parties is a protocol producing a common shared classical key K such that:
 (i) Correctness: all honest parties output the same K;
 (ii) Security: any external eavesdropper learns negligible information about K;
 (iii) Strong fairness under collusion: for every proper subset S ⊊ {1,…,n} of dishonest participants (possibly all but one honest party), the colluding set S cannot bias, predetermine, or determine K alone, and every honest party contributes equally to K;
 (iv) The protocol may be analyzed in three security models: device-dependent (DD), measurement-device-independent (MDI), and semi-device-independent (SDI);
 (v) The protocol may be deployed on different network architectures: star (one central node connected to n−1 leaves), tree (general rooted tree topology), and hybrid (combinations thereof, possibly client–server).

Open problem: Construct an MQKA protocol in which the fundamental entangled resource consumed in each round is a Dicke state |D^n_k⟩ (rather than GHZ or Bell states), and rigorously prove that it satisfies correctness, security, and strong fairness against any collusion of up to n−1 participants, with security and fairness guarantees comparable to existing GHZ-based and Bell-based MQKA protocols. Furthermore, characterize quantitatively, as functions of (n,k), the protocol's:
 (a) qubit efficiency (key bits per transmitted qubit),
 (b) asymptotic and finite-size key rates under realistic channel noise and loss,
 (c) noise and loss tolerance thresholds,
 (d) resilience to collusion of size up to n−1,
 (e) performance trade-offs across the star, tree, and hybrid architectures, and
 (f) achievable security guarantees in each of the DD, MDI, and SDI models.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals an active literature on multiparty quantum key agreement and on fair MQKA protocols resistant to collusive attacks, but these protocols are based on GHZ states, Bell pairs, single qubits, or post-selected GHZ states (in the MDI variant). No published protocol uses Dicke states |D^n_k⟩ as the fundamental entangled resource together with proofs of strong fairness, security, and architecture/security-model characterization. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: New Fair Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement Secure against Collusive Attacks
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a fair MQKA resistant to collusive attacks, based on GHZ-type resources, not Dicke states.
status_evidence.claim: Existing fair MQKA constructions use GHZ/Bell-style resources rather than Dicke states.

status_evidence.title: Measurement-device-independent multi-party quantum key agreement
status_evidence.snippet: MDI MQKA protocol exploiting post-selected GHZ states to ensure fairness.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art MDI MQKA uses GHZ states; no Dicke-state analog is presented.

status_evidence.title: Secure multiparty quantum key agreement against collusive attacks
status_evidence.snippet: Secure MQKA against collusion using non-Dicke resources.
status_evidence.claim: Recent collusion-secure MQKA work does not use Dicke states as the fundamental resource.
